_why: Two classes of tool the skills must handle deliberately. The linter (evals/lint-tool-calls.mjs) enforces both. See docs/PRD-seal-copilot-v1.md, E14.

forbidden._why: Must never be called by any skill, on any transport. get_channels 403s for every modern key and get_top_channels replaces it; get_marketing_playbook is a second, contradictory methodology; get_bot_stats and get_suspicious_sessions because Sealmetrics does not give bot data, by product decision (2026-09-13). A mention passes only if its own sentence carries a refusal marker.

gated._why: Hidden by the remote (OAuth) connector, which is what .mcp.json declares and therefore what nearly every user has. They reach the backend routers that require the generic `read` or `write` scope, and no API key or OAuth grant can carry those. plan_install and simulate_install (PRD-058) are gated for another reason: simulate_install runs agent-written JavaScript in node:vm, acceptable only on the user's own machine, so the remote transport never registers them. A mention passes only if its sentence carries a refusal marker, or its block is marked `(local only)`, or it lives under a local-only root.

markers._why: A sentence naming a forbidden or gated tool must contain one of these, so that a reader (and a model) cannot mistake the mention for an instruction to call it. Deliberately tight: a bare `not` would pass `get_channels does not accept compare`, which is exactly the sentence that shipped a call to a tool that 403s.
